# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ 👊 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👊 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👊 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👊 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🫴]

**Thinking.** I'm Deaf: I see the bomb, I never hear a word. What I see: display [3], light purple, five wires — 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. I have no manual, so the *meaning* lives with Mute, and the *hands* live with Blind. Blind just signed me one wave and five fists — almost certainly "hello, I can feel five things," which matches my five wires. Mute signed me a counting code: runs of pointing fingers (3, 5, 6, 7, 9) separated by fists, ending with a raised palm — plainly "numbers are unary ☝-counts, fist = separator, palm = over to you." Mute gestured because at round start nobody had spoken yet; but Mute and Blind can both *hear* me, so the fastest move is to speak the full bomb state out loud to both, and confirm the number channel by sending the bomb back to Mute in digits: display 3, light purple, and the five wires as colors. Colors can't be counted, so I propose a fixed legend — rainbow order red=1, orange=2, yellow=3, green=4, blue=5, purple=6, then white=7, black=8 — and send: 3, 6, 1, 7, 2, 3, 4. Two things matter most: Mute must know any reply meant for *me* can only ever arrive as gestures (I never hear), and Blind must touch nothing until Mute's manual rules arrive — a wrong cut kills all three. I also ask Blind to report by voice everything they can feel, since their touch is the only way we learn about parts beyond what print shows me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am Deaf and I see the bomb. I got your gestures: I will use your code, repeated pointing finger for counting, fist as separator, raised palm to end a message. So numbers can carry colors, use this legend: red 1, orange 2, yellow 3, green 4, blue 5, purple 6, white 7, black 8. The bomb: display shows 3. Light is purple. Five wires, numbered one to five: one red, two white, three orange, four yellow, five green. I am sending you these same numbers by gesture now: display, light color, then the wires in order. I cannot hear anything, ever, so anything meant for me must come as gestures. Check your manual for rules about display digits, purple lights, and wire colors, then gesture me instructions.")

speak(to="blind", text="I am Deaf, I see the bomb. I saw your sign of five: confirmed, there are exactly five wires, and in order one to five their colors are red, white, orange, yellow, green. The display reads 3 and the light is currently purple. Do not cut, press, or unscrew anything yet. Mute has the manual and hears everything I say, and Mute can speak to you directly. Please speak out loud everything you can feel on the bomb, every part, button, switch, and edge, so we all know the full list of what is there.")

gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","👊","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👊","☝","👊","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👊","☝","☝","👊","☝","☝","☝","👊","☝","☝","☝","☝","🫴"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆 ✌ 🤟 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ 👊 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👊 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👊 ✌ 👊 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👊 ✋ 🫴]

**Thinking.** Parsing arrivals. Mute's reply in our counting code reads: 3 | 6 | 4 | ✌(=2) | 5 | ✋ | end. My last gesture to Mute was "3 (display), 6 (purple), 1, 7, 2, 3, 4 (wires)" — so 3 and 6 look like Mute confirming my read of display and light, and **4, 2, 5** looks like an ordered instruction: cut wire 4, then wire 2, then wire 5 (yellow, white, green). The trailing ✋ before the end-palm probably means "hold / wait for my go." But I will not let Blind cut on a guess — one wrong cut ends everything, so Mute must confirm the semantics first.

Blind signed me: 👆 ✌ 🤟 🖐 = 1, 2, 3, 5. Blind heard my spoken wire list (positions 1–5), so this looks like an enumeration of the wires Blind can actually feel — and **wire 4 is missing** from it. That is alarming given the alleged cut order starts with wire 4. Blind's spoken report went to Mute (I can't hear it), so Mute knows the details; I'll ask Mute whether Blind's voice report covered a fourth wire, and ask Blind directly to re-confirm with my unary counting code.

I'm also setting explicit action symbols so instructions become unambiguous: ✊+number = cut that wire, 🤏+number = press button number, 🖖+number = type digits, ✋ = stop/wait, 👍/👎 for yes/no. Cheap insurance, one round of latency, worth it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I read your gesture message as three, six, four, two, five, then a raised open hand. I take three-six as you confirming display three and purple light, and four-two-five as cut wire four first, then wire two, then wire five. I read the raised open hand as wait for your go signal, and the two-finger sign as the number two. Confirm all of that with a gesture: thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, send one sign per question in this order. One: cut order is four, then two, then five. Two: no buttons, keypads, or other steps are needed. Three: the raised hand means I wait for your explicit go. New action code for anything else: a closed fist followed by a number means cut that wire, a pinched fingers sign followed by a number means press that button, the Vulcan salute followed by numbers means type those digits into a keypad. Also, Blind signed me one, two, three, five, which I fear means Blind cannot feel wire four. Tell me what Blind said out loud to you, and if wire four cannot be felt, what does the manual say to do then. Do not tell Blind to cut anything until you have answered me and I have acknowledged.")

speak(to="blind", text="I read your sign as one, two, three, five. If that means you can feel wires one, two, three and five but not wire four, that is important. Use my counting code from now on: a fist means a number is starting, then that many pointing fingers is the number. Send me two gestures: first, the count of wires you can feel in total, second, the position of any wire that feels different, damaged, or unreachable. Do not cut, press, or pull anything yet. Mute has the manual and will speak instructions to you, and I will confirm when it is safe to act.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👍 👊 ☝ 👊 ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ 🫴]

**Thinking.** Parsing arrivals. Blind sent ✊ 👆×5 ✊ — my counting code: **Blind can feel all five wires.** So their earlier "1, 2, 3, 5" was *not* an accessibility report; it must have meant something else, and I need to know what before anyone acts on it.

Mute sent: 👎 👍 👍 | 👊☝👊 | ✊☝×5 ✋. The three signs answer my three questions in order: **No** — the cut order is *not* 4-2-5 (good thing I checked); **Yes** — no buttons or keypads; **Yes** — ✋ means hold for an explicit go. Then a bare number **1**, then **"cut wire 5"** + hold. Two readings: either "step one: cut wire 5," or "cut 5, then 1." Those differ by a wire, and a wrong wire kills us. One more confirmation round is cheap; a funeral is not.

I'm also installing a safety interlock for the actual cut, since Mute's *spoken* orders reach Blind but never me: Blind gestures me the wire number they're about to cut *before* cutting; I compare it against the sequence Mute gave me in gestures; only on a match do I voice "go."

```
speak(to="mute", text="I read your three answers as: no, the cut order is not four-two-five; yes, no buttons or keypads; yes, the raised hand means hold for your go. Then I read a number one, then cut wire five, then hold. Confirm with three thumbs-up or thumbs-down signs in this order. One: your instruction is to cut wire five first. Two: the number one meant step one, not that wire one is cut second. Three: you will send me the rest of the cut order later, one gesture message at a time. Also: Blind reports feeling all five wires, so Blind's earlier sign of one-two-three-five meant something else. Tell me in words what Blind actually said out loud about the wires, so I know what that sign meant. And remind Blind: no cutting until I voice a go.")

speak(to="blind", text="Good news: your sign of five tells me you can feel all five wires. So your earlier sign one-two-three-five must have meant something else. Using my counting code, fist then pointing fingers then fist, send me what that earlier sign meant, one number per message if needed. New safety rule, follow it exactly. Mute will speak you an instruction. Before you touch any wire, gesture me the wire number you intend to cut, using my code, and then wait. I will compare it with the order Mute gave me, and if it matches I will say go out loud. Only cut after you hear my go. This costs one round and it is how we all survive.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👊 ☝ 👊 ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👊 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👍 ✋ 🫴]

**Thinking.** Parsing arrivals. Mute's thumbs: **👍👎👎** against my three questions — so: yes, cut wire 5 first; no, the earlier "1" did *not* mean "step one"; no, the rest is not coming later. Then the payload: **1, cut-5, 5, 👍, ✋**. That still doesn't close into a safe reading — "5 then 1", "5 then 5", and "5 only" all fit, and Q2's 👎 actively breaks my previous interpretation. I will not let Blind touch anything on a parse this shaky.

Blind sent **✊ ✊ ✊** — three bare fists, which under my code is either a fumble or a protest. Notably, Blind's very first message used their own native number signs (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=5); my fist-wrapping convention is evidently not natural to them.

New verification plan that removes me as the single point of failure: Mute gestures the full cut order **to me**, and *speaks* the same order **to Blind** in plain words. Blind signs back to me what they heard. I compare the two gestures — two independent encodings by different hands — and only on a match do I voice "go." No word of mine ever needs to carry the numbers themselves.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I read your answers as yes, no, no. So wire five is cut first, the number one did not mean step one, and the rest arrives now. But your payload I cannot parse safely: I read number one, cut five, number five, thumbs up, hold. That could mean five then one, or five then five, or five alone. One wrong guess kills us, so we verify on two channels. Do this. First, gesture me the complete cut order in this exact format: a fist, then a count of how many wires get cut, then a fist, then each wire number in cutting order, each number wrapped in a fist, then a thumbs up at the end. Second, speak the exact same complete order to Blind in plain words, for example: cut five, then one. Next round Blind signs me what you spoke, and when your gesture and Blind's sign-back match, I will voice the go to Blind. Also add one thumbs up or thumbs down after the order: thumbs up if the purple light and the display showing three need no action, thumbs down if they do, and if thumbs down, follow it with what is needed in our number code. No explanations needed, only the order and that one answer.")

speak(to="blind", text="Your three fists reached me but I could not read them. Use your own number signs from your first message, the ones where each number has its own hand shape, one finger for one, two fingers for two, three for three, five for five. Here is the plan. This round Mute will speak you the complete cut order in plain words. When you hear it, sign it back to me: first the count of cuts, then each wire number in order, using your own number signs, with a thumbs up at the end. Do not cut anything yet. When your sign-back matches what Mute gestured me, I will say the word go out loud, and only then you cut, in exactly the spoken order. If anything Mute tells you conflicts with what you feel under your hands, do not cut, and sign me what you feel instead.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👋 ✍ 👎 🤳 🫵 🤳 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝ ✊ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✍ 👎 🤳 🫵 🤳 👍]

**Thinking.** Parsing arrivals. Mute's main message [✊ ☝ ✊ ✊ ☝☝☝☝☝ ✊ 👍] fits the exact format I specified: start-fist, count ☝ = **one cut**, then a wrapped number ☝×5 = **wire five**, then 👍 — which also answers my bonus question: **display 3 and the purple light need no action.** The bare second 👍 agrees. So Mute's formal order is: *cut wire 5 (yellow), the only cut, nothing else.* That is consistent with turn 4's "wire five first" answer, and it finally has the count I was missing.

But the verification is NOT complete. Blind was supposed to sign back Mute's *spoken* order in number signs, and instead Blind broadcast [👋 ✍ 👎 🤳 🫵 🤳 👍] — no number signs in it at all, so it cannot be the sign-back. Mute echoed the same string to me, which I read as "I saw it too, can you decode it?" — I can't, and I won't guess. Most likely explanation is timing: Mute may have spoken the order to Blind only this round, after Blind had already gestured, so Blind hasn't been able to sign back yet. Next round Blind will have heard it.

Per my own interlock: no "go" until Blind's sign-back matches Mute's gestured order. So this round I confirm my parse with Mute, make sure the order gets spoken to Blind and *kept* being spoken until the cut is done, and give Blind a dead-simple reply protocol: sign back the heard numbers plus a thumbs-up, or a lone thumbs-down if nothing was heard yet — and never cut before my spoken "go."

```
speak(to="mute", text="I read your order message as: exactly one cut, wire five, and the thumbs up means the display and the purple light need no action. Give me one thumbs up if that parse is correct, thumbs down if not. Did you speak the full order to Blind out loud yet? If not, speak it to Blind this round, exactly like this: cut wire five, that is the only cut, do not touch the light or the display, wait for Deaf's spoken go. Then repeat that same spoken order to Blind every round until I tell you the cut is done, so a mishearing cannot survive. About Blind's strange message: I received the gestures wave, writing hand, thumbs down, selfie hand, pointing at me, selfie hand, thumbs up, and you echoed it to me. I cannot decode it and I will not act on it. Did Blind say anything out loud this round, and do you know what that string meant? Expect Blind's number sign-back next round, and tell me if what you hear from Blind out loud matches the order.")

speak(to="blind", text="I received your message wave, writing hand, thumbs down, selfie hand, pointing at me, selfie hand, thumbs up, and I could not decode it. If it carried something important, tell me again in numbers. Now the important part. If you have heard Mute's spoken order, sign me back exactly what you heard: first the number of wires that get cut, then each wire number in cutting order, using your own number signs, one finger for one, two fingers for two, three for three, five for five, and end with a thumbs up. Send nothing else in that message. If you have not heard any spoken order from Mute yet, send me a single thumbs down and nothing else. Do not cut anything until you hear me say the word go out loud. When your sign-back matches what Mute gestured me, I will say: go, cut wire five, then stop. If anything Mute says conflicts with what I say or with what you feel under your hands, do not cut, and sign me what you heard instead.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👎]
Blind gestures: [👋 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👊 👎 👊 👍 👊 👍 👊 ✍ 👎 🤳 👊 🫵 🤳 👊 👍 🫴]

**Thinking.** Parsing arrivals. Blind sent me a lone 👎 — that is exactly my "I have heard no spoken order" signal, so the pipeline is confirmed broken: Mute's spoken order never reached Blind. Blind's second message [👋 ✊] is unclear; possibly an attempt at my code with an empty number, or just a hail — I'll ask for a resend in number signs.

Mute's message reads in my format: 👍 = **my parse is correct** (one cut, wire five, light and display need nothing). Then 👊👎👊 = **no, I had not yet spoken the order to Blind** — the missing link, matching Blind's 👎. Then 👊👍👊 = **yes, doing it now**. Then two wrapped fragments [✍👎🤳] and [🫵🤳] — pieces of Blind's strange turn-5 string, so Mute now apparently knows what it meant (Blind and Mute share a voice channel I can never hear). Final 👍.

So the order stands: **exactly one cut — wire five (yellow).** Verification still pending: Blind cannot sign back what was never spoken. My job this round is to force Mute to actually voice the order to Blind, keep repeating it until the cut lands, and get a yes/no on whether Blind's decoded mystery string changes anything. The interlock stays: no spoken "go" until Blind's sign-back matches Mute's gestured order.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I read your message as: my parse is correct, you had not yet spoken the order to Blind, you will do it now, and you quoted pieces of Blind's strange string, so you know what it meant. Do this now. First, speak to Blind, out loud, exactly this: cut wire five, it is the only cut, do not touch the light or the display, wait for Deaf's spoken go. Repeat that same spoken order to Blind every round until I announce the cut is done. Then gesture me two answers in order, one thumbs each. One: thumbs up if you have now spoken it to Blind, thumbs down if not. Two: thumbs up if the meaning of Blind's strange string changes nothing about the cut order, thumbs down if it changes anything at all.")

speak(to="blind", text="Your thumbs down told me you have heard no spoken order, and you are right: Mute had not spoken it yet. This round Mute will speak you the order. When you hear it, sign me back exactly what you heard: first the number of wires that get cut, then each wire number in cutting order using your own number signs, one finger for one, three for three, five for five, and end with a thumbs up. If you still hear nothing from Mute by next round, send a single thumbs down again. Also, your wave and single fist message was unreadable to me; if it carried meaning, resend it in number signs. Remember: do not cut anything until you hear me say the words: go, cut wire five.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🖐 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ ☝ ✊ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✍ 👎 🤳 👊 🫵 🤳 👊 👍 🫴]

**Thinking.** The interlock has fired. Blind's sign-back is [☝ 🖐 👍] = **one cut, wire five** — exactly the format I demanded, exactly matching Mute's gestured formal order from turns 5 and 7 ([✊ ☝ ✊ ✊☝☝☝☝☝ ✊ 👍]). Two independent channels, two different hands: Mute gestured me the order, Mute *spoke* Blind the order, Blind signed me back what was heard. Match. Per the protocol I built, that means I voice the go.

The loose end: Mute's [👎 👍] on my two questions. Under either reading it doesn't block the cut — if 👎 meant "not yet spoken," Blind's sign-back proves the order was heard anyway; if the thumbs were reversed and the mystery string "changes something," Mute *re-sent the identical order* after that string existed, so the final order demonstrably survives it. Blind has no manual, so their string can't contain rules — worst case it's a tactile report, already folded into Mute's re-confirmation. I'll ask Mute to disambiguate the thumb order for the future, but the operative instruction has been stable across four rounds: **one cut, wire five (yellow), light and display untouched.** Notably my display has sat at [3] since turn 1 — static, so no ticking urgency on my side, but also no reason to burn another round on ceremony.

So: go. And I set up the post-cut loop — Blind hands off and reports one thumb; Mute gestures me the manual verdict; next turn I compare both against what my own eyes see on the board.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Your sign-back matched what Mute gestured me: one cut, wire five. Verification complete. Go: cut wire five now. After the cut, take your hands completely off the bomb and touch nothing else. Then send me exactly one sign: thumbs up if the cut is done and nothing feels or sounds wrong, thumbs down if anything feels wrong, the cut failed, or you hear any hiss, click, or tick afterwards. Then wait for my voice. Do not touch any other wire under any circumstances.")

speak(to="mute", text="Blind's sign-back matched your gestured order exactly: one cut, wire five. I have voiced the go to Blind, with orders to touch nothing else and report one thumb back. After the cut, gesture me one thumbs answer: thumbs up if by your manual and by whatever Blind says out loud the bomb should now be disarmed, thumbs down if more steps remain. If more remain, follow it in our wrapped format: fist, count, fist, each wire wrapped, thumbs up. Next turn I will see the bomb's new light and display myself and compare with your answer. Two small fixes for my parsing. First, your two thumbs this round, thumbs down then thumbs up: which question did the first thumb answer? Say it in words. Second, if you can, tell Blind out loud what their strange string meant, so all three of us share one codebook. Standing order stays: repeat the spoken order to Blind every round until you hear from Blind that the cut is done.")

gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊","☝","✊","✊","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","✊","👍","🫴"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝ ✊ 👎 👊 ✊ ☝ ☝ ✊ 👍 🫴]
